Tree — leaves#

Leaf geometry and primitives.

class Function : public Leaf#
#include <function.h>

A function geometry primitive/ leaf node.

This is analogs to an F-rep. Functions can be defined in cartesian, cylindrical, or spherical coordinates.

The function is defined by a string that is a math expression. The node uses the exprtk library and therefore can use any operations defined within its parser. The string can contain the following variables:

  • Cartesian coordinates: x, y, and z

  • Cylindrical coordinates: rho, phic, and z

  • Spherical coordinates: r, theta, and phis

Note

phic corresponds to phi in cylindrical and phis to phi in spherical

Note

This node can be evaluated in O(n) time, where N is the number of tokens in the expressions.

Public Functions

virtual std::shared_ptr<Node> clone() final#

Clones the node and returns a new instance of the node.

Note

This may be called before or after prepare() is called, however it is always more efficient to call it after. This is because the prepare() function must be called on all clones of the node separately. If you call prepare() first and then clone the node, the clone() operation will copy from memory instead of re-reading from disk.

Returns:

A new instance of the node

inline virtual DistanceAccuracy distance_accuracy() const override#

How faithfully this node’s value, including its whole subtree, matches the true signed distance.

Composes the node’s own operation with its children’s accuracy, so the root’s answer describes the whole tree. exact and bound promise that the value clamped to the bandwidth is lipschitz_bound()-Lipschitz and that values outside the bounding box are at least the per-axis distance to it (see DistanceAccuracy). Only valid after prepare(); some nodes decide from what prepare()

measured. The default is approximate, so a node without an override can only disable optimizations that rely on the guarantee.

Always approximate: the field is an arbitrary user expression or callback. Nothing bounds how fast a user function changes or whether it measures distance at all (a TPMS or a scaled distance is a common input), so no Lipschitz bound can be promised.

Returns:

The accuracy of the subtree rooted at this node.

class Mesh : public Leaf#
#include <mesh.h>

A mesh geometry primitive/ leaf node.

The mesh is loaded from a file and converted into a signed distance field using OpenVDB.

Mesh files are loaded into triangles/ vertices using the Assimp library when the node is constructed. prepare() then converts the triangles into an OpenVDB narrow-band signed distance grid at a resolution derived from the voxel size, and evaluate() returns the interpolated distance to the mesh. Attributes are set on the node like any other leaf.

The value: prepare() stores distances within bandwidth + |sdf_shim| of the surface (the band value beyond it), so the shimmed value is valid out to the bandwidth on both sides. Inside the bounding box padded by the bandwidth, evaluate() returns max(F, d), where F is the grid interpolated trilinearly minus sdf_shim and d the signed Euclidean distance to the bounding box; beyond the padded box it returns no value. A positive sdf_shim grows the bounding box by the shim (the grown part stays inside it); a negative one keeps the mesh’s box. Inside the box d only lifts values that fall below minus the distance to the box, which a true distance never does, and never changes their sign; outside it, d removes interpolated material beyond the box.

Distance accuracy (distance_accuracy()): bound, with the Lipschitz bound prepare() measures on its grid (SurfaceMesh::sdf_lipschitz_bound(), at least 1): the largest trilinear gradient over every grid cell the padded box reads, including inactive voxels, tiles and the background. d is at least the bandwidth on the faces of the padded box, so the band-clipped value runs continuously into the early-out, and outside the box every value is at least the distance to it. The bound holds for the implemented surface (the grid’s own sign), whatever the mesh’s quality. approximate before prepare(), or if the measurement fails.

Note

The Mesh class is only available if the Assimp and OpenVDB libraries are available.

Note

This node can be evaluated in O(1) time.

Node-specific part of prepare(), called after the bandwidth has been recorded.

Composite nodes prepare their children here. The base implementation does nothing.

Builds the signed distance grid from the mesh loaded by the constructor and measures its Lipschitz bound. The grid voxel size is the override voxel size if given, else the sample size if given, else the requested voxel size clamped to at least 0.5% of the smallest bounding-box dimension.

class TexturedMesh : public Leaf#
#include <textured_mesh.h>

A closed textured triangle solid with an intrinsic volumetric COLOR_RGBA field.

TexturedMesh imports 3MF Materials/Properties or OBJ/MTL appearance data and converts the surface appearance during prepare() into a sparse inward color shell. Shell colors are extended from the closest surface point; deeper samples use the configured opaque core color. Geometry is prepared as an OpenVDB signed-distance grid.

The value follows Mesh: inside the bounding box padded by the bandwidth, evaluate() returns max(F, d), F the grid interpolated trilinearly and d the signed Euclidean distance to the bounding box, and no value beyond it. The grid’s exterior band reaches the prepared bandwidth (or sqrt(3) voxels, if wider).

Distance accuracy (distance_accuracy()): bound, with the Lipschitz bound prepare() measures on the grid (SurfaceMesh::sdf_lipschitz_bound(), at least 1), for the same reasons as Mesh; approximate before prepare() or if the measurement fails. Colors and other attributes are only sampled where the value is at most zero.

Note

3MF model units are converted to millimeters. OBJ coordinates are multiplied by obj_unit_scale because OBJ does not define physical units.

Note

Source alpha is deliberately ignored. COLOR_RGBA is always emitted with alpha 1.

Warning

prepare() must be called before evaluate() or sample().

class Strut : public Leaf#
#include <strut.h>

A leaf node that represents a strut.

A strut is the conical frustum swept between a start and an end point, with an independent radius at each end, closed by a capping mode at each end. When both radii are equal and both ends are sphere capped, the strut is a capsule.

Note

The geometry follows the 3MF Beam Lattice Extension definition of a beam: the frustum is built between the two vertices and then unioned with the requested end caps.

Public Types

enum class CapMode#

How a strut end is closed off.

Mirrors ST_CapMode from the 3MF Beam Lattice Extension.

Values:

enumerator Sphere#

The end is closed with a full sphere of the end radius.

enumerator HemiSphere#

The end is closed with the outward half of a sphere of the end radius.

enumerator Butt#

The end is closed flat, leaving a cylindrical or conical shape.

Public Functions

Note

This is because the prepare() function must be called on all clones of the node separately. If you call prepare() first and then clone the node, the clone() operation will copy from memory instead of re-reading from disk.

Returns:

A new instance of the node

inline virtual Node::DiagramFamily diagram_family() const override#

Returns the semantic style family used for this node in Mermaid diagrams.

Concrete OpenVCAD nodes should override this. The base fallback exists for mocks and other internal helper nodes that do not need custom diagram metadata.

Returns:

The diagram family. The base implementation returns DiagramFamily::composition.

inline virtual std::string diagram_label() const override#

Concrete OpenVCAD nodes should override this. The base fallback exists for mocks and other internal helper nodes that do not need custom diagram metadata.

Returns:

The node’s type name, e.g. “Sphere”. The base implementation returns “Node”.

virtual DistanceAccuracy distance_accuracy() const override#

How faithfully this node’s value, including its whole subtree, matches the true signed distance.

Composes the node’s own operation with its children’s accuracy, so the root’s answer describes the whole tree. exact and bound promise that the value clamped to the bandwidth is lipschitz_bound()-Lipschitz and that values outside the bounding box are at least the per-axis distance to it (see DistanceAccuracy). Only valid after prepare(); some nodes decide from what prepare()

measured. The default is approximate, so a node without an override can only disable optimizations that rely on the guarantee.

How faithfully the value matches the true distance, by cap configuration.

  • exact: a capsule (equal radii, sphere caps), a frustum with butt caps at both ends, and a degenerate (zero-length) strut without butt caps (a ball);

  • bound, Lipschitz bound 1: a frustum with sphere caps at either end otherwise. The caps are joined by min, which is exact outside and underestimates the depth inside;

  • approximate: a hemisphere at the wider end. The hemisphere is gated by the plane through its vertex, so the value jumps inside the material across that plane (from the frustum’s near-zero depth to the sphere’s). Also a degenerate strut with a butt cap, whose ball may not fit the butt end’s box.

Returns:

The accuracy of the subtree rooted at this node.

class CAD : public Leaf#
#include <cad.h>

A CAD geometry primitive/ leaf node.

The CAD is loaded from a file into memory for sampling.

Distance accuracy (distance_accuracy()): in exact mode (use_fast_mode = false) the value is OpenCASCADE’s distance to the B-rep, signed by its solid classifier. prepare() checks the part: when it is one closed shell (every face in it, every edge bounding two faces) and every face and edge is elementary (planes, cylinders, cones, spheres and tori bounded by lines and conics), the distance comes from closed-form extrema and the value is exact. A solid is sewn into its shell; a solid bounded by a single face (a sphere, a torus), which sewing would leave as a loose face with no inside, keeps its own shell. Otherwise exact mode is approximate: free-form (B-spline or offset) geometry uses sampled extrema that can miss the nearest point, an open shape or a loose face has no consistent sign, and unsewn or overlapping bodies are not checked.

Fast mode samples a mesh SDF grid of the tessellated part like Mesh: inside the bounding box padded by the bandwidth, evaluate() returns max(F, d), F the grid interpolated trilinearly and d the signed Euclidean distance to the bounding box, and no value beyond it. It is bound, with the Lipschitz bound prepare() measures on the grid (SurfaceMesh::sdf_lipschitz_bound(), at least 1), for the same reasons as Mesh. Attributes are only sampled where the value is at most zero, in both modes.

Note

The node supports .STEP and .igs files.

class Cylinder : public Leaf#
#include <cylinder.h>

A cylinder leaf node/ geometric primitive.

This node is a capped cylinder with a center point, radius, and height. Its axis is parallel to the Z axis and passes through the center, and it spans center.z - height / 2 to center.z + height / 2. The evaluate() function returns the signed distance to the surface.

Note

This node can be evaluated in O(1) time.

Note

This node is a leaf node, and therefore cannot have any children.

Public Functions

Returns the center point of the Cylinder.

Returns:

The center point of the Cylinder.

Clones the node and returns a new instance of the node.

Note

This may be called before or after prepare() is called, however it is always more efficient to call it after. This is because the prepare() function must be called on all clones of the node separately. If you call prepare() first and then clone the node, the clone() operation will copy from memory instead of re-reading from disk.

Returns:

A new instance of the node

class Torus : public Leaf#
#include <torus.h>

A torus leaf node/ geometric primitive.

This node is a torus with a major and minor radius. See this for more information: https://wiki.povray.org/uploaded/2/29/RefImgMimxrtor.gif The major radius is the distance from the center of the torus to the center of the tube. The minor radius is the radius of the tube. The torus is centered at the origin with its ring in the XY plane, so its axis of symmetry is Z.

How faithfully this node’s value, including its whole subtree, matches the true signed distance.

Composes the node’s own operation with its children’s accuracy, so the root’s answer describes the whole tree. exact and bound promise that the value clamped to the bandwidth is lipschitz_bound()-Lipschitz and that values outside the bounding box are at least the per-axis distance to it (see DistanceAccuracy). Only valid after prepare(); some nodes decide from what prepare()

measured. The default is approximate, so a node without an override can only disable optimizations that rely on the guarantee.

Exact for a ring or horn torus (r2 <= r1), bound with Lipschitz bound 1 for a spindle torus. The value |(|xy| - r1, z)| - r2 is 1-Lipschitz and is the exact distance outside every torus. Inside a spindle torus (r2 > r1, r1 > 0) the tube circle crosses the axis, so the depth near the axis is underestimated: a bound. r1 = 0 is a sphere (exact). Negative radii describe no torus, so they promise nothing (approximate).

Returns:

The accuracy of the subtree rooted at this node.

virtual DistanceAccuracy distance_accuracy() const override#

How faithfully this node’s value, including its whole subtree, matches the true signed distance.

Composes the node’s own operation with its children’s accuracy, so the root’s answer describes the whole tree. exact and bound promise that the value clamped to the bandwidth is lipschitz_bound()-Lipschitz and that values outside the bounding box are at least the per-axis distance to it (see DistanceAccuracy). Only valid after prepare(); some nodes decide from what prepare()

measured. The default is approximate, so a node without an override can only disable optimizations that rely on the guarantee.

bound, sharp or blended: the value is the larger of the strut union and the exact distance to the lattice box. The union is the sorted quadratic fold of exact capsule distances, which is 1-Lipschitz, and the members it skips are far enough that they cannot move it within the bandwidth. The box term keeps every value outside the box at least the distance to it, however far a blend of several struts dips.

class BeamLattice : public Leaf#
#include <beam_lattice.h>

A leaf node representing a beam-and-ball lattice defined over a shared vertex list.

BeamLattice implements the geometry model of the 3MF Beam Lattice Extension. Beams index into a shared vertex list and carry optional per-end radii and cap modes that fall back to the lattice defaults. Balls are spheres centred on vertices. Every beam and ball becomes a child of an internal accelerated union, so large lattices stay cheap to sample.

Note

Beams shorter than min_length are dropped, as the specification requires consumers to ignore them.

Warning

prepare() must be called before evaluate() or sample(). bounding_box() is safe before prepare(); the box is computed in the constructor.

Public Types

enum class BallMode#

Whether balls are generated at beam vertices.

Mirrors ST_BallMode from the 3MF Beam Lattice Extension.

Values:

enumerator None#

No balls are created.

enumerator Mixed#

Balls are created only at vertices with an explicit ball entry.

enumerator All#

Balls are created at every vertex that terminates a surviving beam.

using CapMode = Strut::CapMode#

Capping mode applied to a beam end.

class ThreeMFBeamLattice : public Leaf#
#include <three_mf_beam_lattice.h>

A leaf node that imports a 3MF Beam Lattice Extension file as an implicit tree.

Each imported object becomes a BeamLattice unioned with the object’s triangle shell. A lattice with a clipping mode is intersected with, or subtracted from, its clipping mesh, so the imported geometry matches what a conforming consumer would produce. Coordinates are converted to millimeters and build transforms are applied.

Note

This importer covers geometry only. Per-beam and per-ball property references (pid, p1, p2) are not read, so imported lattices carry no material or color attributes.

Warning

prepare() must be called before evaluate() or sample(). bounding_box() is safe before prepare(); the box is computed in the constructor.

virtual DistanceAccuracy distance_accuracy() const override#

How faithfully this node’s value, including its whole subtree, matches the true signed distance.

Composes the node’s own operation with its children’s accuracy, so the root’s answer describes the whole tree. exact and bound promise that the value clamped to the bandwidth is lipschitz_bound()-Lipschitz and that values outside the bounding box are at least the per-axis distance to it (see DistanceAccuracy). Only valid after prepare(); some nodes decide from what prepare()

measured. The default is approximate, so a node without an override can only disable optimizations that rely on the guarantee.

Composes the imported pieces: each

BeamLattice and Mesh reports its own accuracy, and the sharp union, clip intersection and clip difference the importer builds keep a bound with the largest L. approximate if any piece is, if a printed piece (lattice, shell, or representation mesh) reaches outside the import box, or if a clipping mesh’s box misses the lattice box entirely.

Returns:

The accuracy of the subtree rooted at this node.

class MappedImplicitLattice : public Leaf#
#include <mapped_implicit_lattice.h>

A metric-corrected periodic implicit unit cell evaluated through a CellMap.

At a world point the unit cell’s value is evaluated at the point’s logical coordinates and divided by the length of its gradient pulled back through the map’s Jacobian, which gives a first-order world-space distance to the cell’s zero surface. In “sheet” mode the solid is the wall of that surface, |distance| - thickness / 2; in “solid” mode it is distance - level.

class MappedGraphLattice : public Leaf#
#include <mapped_graph_lattice.h>

A compact native graph lattice tiled and curved through a CellMap.

Struts (and optional joint spheres) are combined with a plain minimum unless a member blend radius is given. Then distinct members are joined with the shared smooth blend (SmoothBlend, quadratic profile, order-independent), which fillets the nodes where struts meet. A member is one strut or one joint in lattice coordinates: the copies of a strut or joint that neighbouring cells share, and the pieces of a strut subdivided to follow a curved map, count as one member and are never blended with each other. The radius may be a field (a ScalarParameter with bounds); where it is 0 the nodes stay sharp. Fillet material takes the nearest member’s component attributes.

virtual DistanceAccuracy distance_accuracy() const override#

How faithfully this node’s value, including its whole subtree, matches the true signed distance.

Composes the node’s own operation with its children’s accuracy, so the root’s answer describes the whole tree. exact and bound promise that the value clamped to the bandwidth is lipschitz_bound()-Lipschitz and that values outside the bounding box are at least the per-axis distance to it (see DistanceAccuracy). Only valid after prepare(); some nodes decide from what prepare()

measured. The default is approximate, so a node without an override can only disable optimizations that rely on the guarantee.

bound when the cell extends the map domain and every element is active, so the solid is not clipped to the map: the value is then the exact minimum over the prepared triangles of the distance minus half the interpolated thickness. approximate otherwise: outside the map domain the value switches to the distance to the domain boundary, which jumps against the lattice value inside.

Returns:

The accuracy of the subtree rooted at this node.

class MappedRim : public Leaf#
#include <mapped_rim.h>

A solid band along the cropped edges of a CellMap, built as a signed distance field from the map’s edge wall.

MappedRim closes off the open lateral edges that trimming leaves on a mapped lattice. The rim is the set of points inside the active map domain that lie within the width field of the map’s edge wall: the smooth trim wall swept from the surface’s cropped boundary through the map height for boundary-trimmed maps, and the exposed lateral element faces otherwise. The band therefore spans the full map height, follows the cropped edge exactly, and extends the sampled width inward, so unioning it with any lattice mapped through the same CellMap seals the lattice’s open edge cells.

The width attribute is sampled through the shared CellMap context, so it can vary with logical position exactly like the other mapped lattice fields.

class CellMapDomain : public Leaf#
#include <cell_map_domain.h>

The active volume of a CellMap as a solid implicit node.

The node’s field is CellMap::domain_signed_distance(): negative inside the active, trimmed map domain, zero on its boundary, and positive outside. Trimmed margins, boundary-trimmed edges, and holes of a surface map are all outside. The boundary is the map’s exposed element faces plus its smooth trim wall, so the distance is exact to that triangulated boundary (about one quarter of an element face in resolution).

Uses: clip any node to a liner volume with an Intersection, use the volume as a host for a stochastic lattice, or subtract it as a keep-out. The node has no internal state to prepare beyond the bounding box, which is the map’s world bounding box.

class StochasticGraphLattice : public Node#
#include <stochastic_graph_lattice.h>

Compact Delaunay or Voronoi graph lattice confined by an implicit host.

World-space seed points are tessellated with CGAL during prepare(). Prepared graph edges use tapered capsule SDFs and an internal BVH. The host is an owned geometry child and is always the authoritative confinement SDF: like every node, the lattice has no value beyond the host’s box padded by the bandwidth, even with seeds outside the host. sample() has the value of evaluate() and evaluates and returns attributes only where that value is <= 0.

Warning

prepare() must be called before evaluate(), sample(), or product inspection.

  • prune_loose_fragments – Drop strut pieces that the host cuts off at both ends (chords through a corner or a concave part of the host, which would print as loose pieces), edges that never enter the host, and joints centred outside it.

  • allow_outside_seeds – Accept seeds outside the host (but inside a finite working box). A layer of such seeds bounds the Voronoi cells at the host surface; the host still confines all geometry.

class Text : public Leaf#
#include <text.h>

A text leaf node which generates a 3D text object by extruding the text along the Z-axis.

Generates a 3D text object from a given string by creating a planar CAD outline in the XY plane, anchored at the origin, and extruding it along Z, centered so it spans -depth / 2 to depth / 2.

Note

The default font is Consolas. The CAD part is built in the constructor; prepare() builds the voxelized distance grid that evaluate() reads.

inline virtual DistanceAccuracy distance_accuracy() const override#

How faithfully this node’s value, including its whole subtree, matches the true signed distance.

Composes the node’s own operation with its children’s accuracy, so the root’s answer describes the whole tree. exact and bound promise that the value clamped to the bandwidth is lipschitz_bound()-Lipschitz and that values outside the bounding box are at least the per-axis distance to it (see DistanceAccuracy). Only valid after prepare(); some nodes decide from what prepare()

measured. The default is approximate, so a node without an override can only disable optimizations that rely on the guarantee.

Approximate: the value is sampled from a grid, not computed from the glyphs.

prepare() tessellates the extruded outline (0.1 deflection) and voxelizes it into an OpenVDB narrow-band level set, which evaluate() interpolates trilinearly. The grid is uniform at the smallest voxel size, its distances and signs come from the voxelizer, and trilinear interpolation is only sqrt(3)-Lipschitz even for exact samples. In practice the value also falls below the per-axis distance to the box and jumps at the edge of the narrow band, so no Lipschitz bound holds.

Returns:

The accuracy of the subtree rooted at this node.

class SignedDistanceField : public Leaf#
#include <signed_distance_field.h>

A leaf node whose signed distance is read from an OpenVDB grid.

The grid can be a FloatGrid of signed distances, a BoolGrid occupancy grid converted to a level set, a FloatVDBVolume, or a grid loaded from a .vdb file. evaluate() interpolates the grid.

Distance accuracy (distance_accuracy()): approximate. The grid is sampled as given: a FloatGrid’s values need not be distances at all, and the narrow band and background are fixed when the grid is built, independent of the prepared bandwidth. With a bandwidth wider than the stored band the value saturates at the background and then jumps to the bandwidth where evaluate() stops returning values, so no Lipschitz bound can be promised.

This may be called before or after prepare() is called, however it is always more efficient to call it after. This is because the prepare() function must be called on all clones of the node separately. If you call prepare() first and then clone the node, the clone() operation will copy from memory instead of re-reading from disk.

Create a SignedDistanceField from a VDB file.

This constructor loads a signed distance field from a specified VDB file path. The VDB file is expected to contain either a BooleanGrid representing an occupancy grid or a FloatGrid representing the signed distance field. We auto-detect the grid type based the type of grid stored in the file. If the grid is a BooleanGrid, it will be converted to a signed distance field. If it’s already a FloatGrid, it will be used directly as the signed distance field. The topology options are used only when the loaded grid is a BooleanGrid. They are ignored for FloatGrid inputs. The default topology option values preserve OpenVCAD’s existing conversion behavior. The grid name can be specified, and it defaults to “occupancy”.

Parameters:

  • vdb_file_path – The file path to the VDB file containing the grid

  • grid_name – The name of the grid to load from the VDB file, default is “occupancy”

  • half_width_voxels – Half the width of the generated narrow-band level set, in voxel units.

  • closing_steps – Number of morphological closing steps used to fill gaps in the active voxel region.

  • dilation_voxels – Number of voxels to expand the active voxel region before conversion.

  • smoothing_steps – Number of smoothing iterations applied after level-set generation.

class SurfaceReliefVolume : public Leaf#
#include <surface_relief_volume.h>

Compact live implicit volume between an embedded selected surface and a raised height map.

For surface q(u,v), outward normal n(u,v), height h(u,v), and embed depth e, this represents q + t*n for -e <= t <= h inside the selected patch. Its zero surface is correct, but the field is not generally an exact Euclidean signed distance when surface curvature or height varies.

Distance accuracy (distance_accuracy()): approximate. The top term t - h(u, v) is as steep as the height field, which an image or a function can make arbitrarily steep, and the closest-point projection behind (u, v), its normal and boundary distance can jump (across mesh edges or the medial axis of a curved patch), so no Lipschitz bound holds.

class PolygonExtrude : public Extrude#
#include <polygon_extrude.h>

An extruded polygon leaf node / geometric primitive.

This node takes a planar polygon defined by a series of 3D points and extrudes it along its computed normal (right-hand rule) by a given height. The polygon must be planar; the constructor validates this and throws if the points are not coplanar. The extrusion can be symmetric (half the height on each side of the polygon plane) or one-directional (full height in the normal direction). A negative height extrudes in the opposite direction of the normal.

PolygonExtrude is the polygon case of Extrude: the vertices become a Profile in the polygon’s own plane, and the plane is placed with a rigid frame. The distance is exact, and the Extrude coordinate fields are available.

Note

This node is a leaf node, and therefore cannot have any children.

class PolygonRevolve : public Revolve#
#include <polygon_revolve.h>

A revolved polygon leaf node / geometric primitive.

This node takes a planar CAD-style half-profile polygon and revolves it around an arbitrary axis line. The axis is defined by two points, and positive partial sweeps follow the right-hand rule of axis_end - axis_start. The profile plane must contain the axis, and all profile vertices must remain on one side of the axis though they may touch it. Partial sweeps are capped at the start and end angles.

PolygonRevolve is the polygon case of Revolve: the vertices become a Profile in (distance from the axis, position along the axis) coordinates, and the axis is placed with a rigid frame. The distance is exact for full and partial sweeps, and the Revolve coordinate fields are available.

Note

Axis-aligned bounding boxes are available before prepare(), but prepare() must still be called before evaluate(), sample(), or other prepared-tree queries.

Note

This node is a leaf node, and therefore cannot have any children.

class Tube : public Leaf#
#include <tube.h>

A tube (pipe) of constant or varying radius along any curve.

The tube is every point within r of the curve, where r is measured at the curve point closest to the query: the signed distance is |p - c(t*)| - r(c(t*)). The radius is a ScalarParameter sampled at c(t*), so it can vary in space (any FloatAttribute) or along the curve: a law on the curve parameter or arc length is a field built from curve_field() / coordinate_field(), for example the normalized length mapped to a radius range.

Ends of open curves: CapMode::Sphere and CapMode::HemiSphere both close the end with a rounded (half-ball) cap; CapMode::Butt cuts it flat, perpendicular to the end tangent. Closed curves have no ends. Strut remains the cheaper choice for a straight tube.

Attributes (new geometry): the node’s own attributes, plus coordinate fields from coordinate_field(): “parameter”, “length”, “normalized_length”, “angle” and “distance”.

Distance accuracy (distance_accuracy()): exact for a straight (LineSegment) tube of constant radius; bound for a curved tube of constant radius; approximate for a field radius (which needs known bounds to size the bounding box) and for butt caps on a curved open curve. With a constant radius the value |p - c(t*)| - r is 1-Lipschitz and exact outside (to the curve’s closest-point accuracy); inside a curved tube it is exact only while the tube is proper (see below), else it underestimates the depth.

The tube stays a proper tube while the radius is smaller than the curve’s radius of curvature; beyond that the surface folds over itself.

This is because the prepare() function must be called on all clones of the node separately. If you call prepare() first and then clone the node, the clone() operation will copy from memory instead of re-reading from disk.

How faithfully this node’s value, including its whole subtree, matches the true signed distance.

Composes the node’s own operation with its children’s accuracy, so the root’s answer describes the whole tree. exact and bound promise that the value clamped to the bandwidth is lipschitz_bound()-Lipschitz and that values outside the bounding box are at least the per-axis distance to it (see DistanceAccuracy). Only valid after prepare(); some nodes decide from what prepare()

measured. The default is approximate, so a node without an override can only disable optimizations that rely on the guarantee.

Exact for a straight constant-radius tube, bound for a curved one, approximate for a field radius or for butt caps on a curved open curve. A curved tube is exact outside but underestimates the depth once the radius passes the curve’s radius of curvature. With a butt cap,

evaluate() takes the flat-end formula when the closest curve point is that end and the plane-clipped tube formula otherwise; on a curved open curve the two disagree where the closest point jumps between the end and the body (a point beyond the end plane equally far from both), so the value jumps there. A straight curve (a LineSegment) or a closed curve has no such jump.

The accuracy of the subtree rooted at this node.

class Extrude : public Leaf#
#include <extrude.h>

A profile extruded from a sketch plane along its normal, with optional draft (taper), twist and a wall offset law.

The profile lies in the plane (by default the XY plane) and is extruded along the plane’s normal from 0 to height (from height up to 0 when height is negative), or from -|height|/2 to |height|/2 when symmetric; below, “z” is the distance along the normal. Draft tapers the walls: the section at height s above the base is the profile offset inward by s * tan(draft) (a negative draft widens it); when symmetric, s is measured from the profile plane both ways. Twist turns the section counter-clockwise about the normal, growing linearly from 0 at the base to twist at the top.

The offset law shapes the walls along the height: points (f, w) say that the section at fraction f of the way from the base to the top is the profile offset outward by w (inward for negative w), joined smoothly between the points (a monotone cubic, PiecewiseCurve) and held at the end values beyond them. It adds to the draft, so a bulge, a waist or a flared foot is a few points.

Attributes (new geometry): the node’s own attributes, plus coordinate fields from coordinate_field(): “u”, “v”, “height”, “normalized_height” and “profile_distance”.

Distance accuracy (distance_accuracy()): exact without draft, twist or offset law (the profile distance is exact). With any of them the wall term is divided by a bound on its slope, sqrt(1 + (omega * rho + |tan(draft)| + lambda)^2), where omega is the twist rate, rho the larger of the point’s and the profile’s distance from the axis and lambda the law’s largest slope, and it is combined with the end caps by max. Beside the walls that value falls below the per-axis distance to the bounding box, so the box promise fails and the value jumps to the band where is_in_bbox() cuts it off: approximate.

Subclassed by PolygonExtrude

Composes the node’s own operation with its children’s accuracy, so the root’s answer describes the whole tree. exact and bound promise that the value clamped to the bandwidth is lipschitz_bound()-Lipschitz and that values outside the bounding box are at least the per-axis distance to it (see DistanceAccuracy). class Revolve : public Leaf#
#include <revolve.h>

A profile revolved about an axis in its sketch plane, fully or through a partial angle.

The profile lies in a sketch plane and turns about the plane’s y axis (through its origin). The profile’s u coordinate (its x) is the distance from the axis and must not be negative; its v coordinate (its y) is the position along the axis. The default plane is SketchPlane::xz(): the axis is world +Z, x is the radius and y becomes z. The sweep starts in the sketch plane (on its +x side) and turns counter-clockwise about the axis through angle_degrees. Profile edges that lie on the axis are interior to the solid, not surfaces. A partial sweep is closed by flat caps.

Attributes (new geometry): the node’s own attributes, plus coordinate fields from coordinate_field(): “u”, “v”, “angle”, “normalized_angle” and “profile_distance”.

Distance accuracy (distance_accuracy()): exact for full and partial sweeps. Inside the swept wedge the distance is the meridian-plane profile distance (and, inside the solid, the distance to the end caps); outside it, the distance to the nearer cap face, which is where the closest point lies because distance along each orbit grows with angle.

Subclassed by PolygonRevolve

class Sweep : public Leaf#
#include <sweep.h>

A profile swept along a path curve.

The profile’s (u, v) plane is carried along the path in its rotation-minimizing frames: u along the frame normal and v along the binormal, so the profile does not twist on its own. For a planar path the binormal is the plane normal unless up says otherwise. The section can be scaled and twisted along the way: scale and twist (in degrees, counter-clockwise about the path tangent) are ScalarParameters sampled at the closest path point, so a law along the path is a field built from the path’s own fields, such as path.length_field(normalized=True). Open paths end in flat caps perpendicular to the end tangents; closed paths close on themselves (the frames are made to meet at the seam).

Attributes (new geometry): the node’s own attributes, plus coordinate fields from coordinate_field(): “parameter”, “length”, “normalized_length”, “u”, “v” and “profile_distance”.

Distance accuracy (distance_accuracy()): exact for a straight path (a LineSegment) with a constant scale and a constant twist (an extrusion of a rigidly turned profile); otherwise approximate. The section of each point is the one at its closest path point, so the profile must stay inside the path’s radius of curvature, as for any swept solid.

Public Functions

virtual std::shared_ptr<Node> clone() override#

Clones the node and returns a new instance of the node.

Note

This may be called before or after prepare() is called, however it is always more efficient to call it after. This is because the prepare() function must be called on all clones of the node separately. If you call prepare() first and then clone the node, the clone() operation will copy from memory instead of re-reading from disk.

Returns:

A new instance of the node

Returns:

inline virtual std::string diagram_label() const override#

Returns the display label used for this node in Mermaid diagrams.

Concrete OpenVCAD nodes should override this. The base fallback exists for mocks and other internal helper nodes that do not need custom diagram metadata.

Returns:

The node’s type name, e.g. “Sphere”. The base implementation returns “Node”.

virtual DistanceAccuracy distance_accuracy() const override#

How faithfully this node’s value, including its whole subtree, matches the true signed distance.

Composes the node’s own operation with its children’s accuracy, so the root’s answer describes the whole tree. exact and bound promise that the value clamped to the bandwidth is lipschitz_bound()-Lipschitz and that values outside the bounding box are at least the per-axis distance to it (see DistanceAccuracy). Only valid after prepare(); some nodes decide from what prepare()

measured. The default is approximate, so a node without an override can only disable optimizations that rely on the guarantee.

Exact for a straight path with constant scale and twist; otherwise approximate. Along a

LineSegment the frame is constant, so a constant scale and twist place one rigidly turned, scaled profile at every closest point: the value is the exact prism distance, and the box (the path box grown by the scaled profile radius) holds it. Elsewhere the section at the closest path point can change abruptly (where the closest point jumps, or with scale and twist laws), so nothing is promised.

Returns:

The accuracy of the subtree rooted at this node.

virtual std::optional<double> evaluate_impl(double x, double y, double z) override#

Node-specific signed distance, called by evaluate() once the node is prepared.

Parameters:

  • x – The x coordinate of the point to evaluate.

  • y – The y coordinate of the point to evaluate.

  • z – The z coordinate of the point to evaluate.

Returns:

The signed distance (negative inside), or an empty optional where the node has no value.

inline virtual double lipschitz_bound() const override#

The Lipschitz bound L that goes with distance_accuracy().

A point whose value v (clamped to the bandwidth) is positive has no inside point within v / L of it. 1 for exact; infinity for approximate. Only valid after prepare().

Returns:

L, at least 1, or infinity when nothing is promised.

class SweepGeometry : public CoordinateSource#
#include <sweep.h>

The evaluation state of a Sweep, shared with its coordinate fields.

Coordinates: “parameter”, “length”, “normalized_length” (of the closest path point), “u” and “v” (profile coordinates, with the scale and twist undone) and “profile_distance” (the signed distance to the scaled, twisted section outline).

struct LocalFrame#
#include <local_frame.h>

A rigid placement: an origin and three orthonormal axes.

Extrude and Revolve work in their own local coordinates (the profile in the local XY plane); PolygonExtrude and PolygonRevolve place those coordinates in the world with a frame. The default is the world frame. Being rigid, it keeps distances exact.
